Tell you what. If it weren't for Dynamic Recon Ops, Dynamic Civil War, OPCOM, and more, Arma 3 would be a waste of money. It is so funny too because, in the main story, you get essentially these mods from "The East Wind". Then when your done with that chapter, it's back to the linear story never to be seen again. 

Give me non-linear randomization to the umpth degree on every map/terrain with an infinite amount of customization via virtual arsenal. That's Dynamic Recon Ops. Then allow me to use mods to actively manage my experience in-game. Spawn in CAS, Artillery, Thunderstorms, Black Holes, Vehicles, Tanks, and etc etc. Thanks to the modding community, Arma 3 has almost limitless replayability. 

Also, Be sure to avoid AI mods. I know, it sounds like a no brainer to want better AI. This may be an exception if you have the latest gen CPU. 

[h3]Setup Tutorial/ Notes for Future Me:[/h3]

First, you've got to, in the Arma 3 launcher, manually set up your parameters like, no logs, world - empty, skip intro, show static background, and no land. That'll make it faster to boot and navigate the menus. Avoid manually typing in and checking the boxes for your hardware and graphics settings like threads, hyperthreading, cpu, ram, and etc. The new 2.20 version fully utilizes your hardware now. Also, using a custom memory allocator can boost your fps, but most people recommend using "system" option. I use and have personally vetted Mimalloc 3.3.2 and in the past v.2.0.7 lock pages. This allocator is meant to be further improved marginally by enabling "Lock Pages" in your OS. This is a locked feature in your OS that unlocks your memory for the game and keeps it from getting swapped by the OS. Kind of niche and will require some know how to get right. Otherwise, just use it without the OS modification.

Turn all of your graphics to extreme and leave Objects to very low. Disable PIP, your CPU takes a heavy load with this one. Something to note, some weapon mods use PIP and you'll need to disable them in the mod options. They usually give you a 2D alternative. Turn v-sync off and run in Fullscreen-Windowed. FSAA coupled with ATOC is good to have on full, but if it helps, disable it entirely. It is a heavy option but looks amazing if your GPU can handle it. Turn Rotational Blur off. It's a heavy hitter with little effect and then put everything else to max. HDAO if your runing AMD GPU and HBAO is your running Nvidia GPU. If your PC specs are anywhere close to mine, you'll be running around 80-100 fps average and 48-68 fps lows in really heavy fights. Thankfully, the lows go rather quickly. The exception would be these CDLCs. Their scenarios are so unoptimized that you'll be lucky to get any FPS. I bought em just for the maps and equipment you get for Faction mods and Dynamic Recon Ops integration. Also, you wont be able to lower GPU based options and expect better performance just because. Arma 3 will push things as much as possible to the CPU. It's only when the game is forced to push the load onto the graphics card is when you start to see an improvement with FPS. So keep those settings on high, utltra, or extreme and you'll most likely see better performance.

Arma 3 does utilize all of your hardware now, but does not manage it very well. It tries to push the load where it can onto your CPU. Force the game to use your GPU by raising the graphics settings on GPU based options. Running mods that rely on your CPU just does not bode well for performance. Any mod that adds in a C++ program code just need to be avoided. Run only a few small mods with them and you'll be fine. But even then, i'd be skeptical.

[h3]Closing Notes:[/h3]

Most FPS mods are mostly outdated and will hurt your fps with the new 2.20 update. Arma 3 can at times, be a bit Janky and there is no shame in using single player cheat mods that help "Manage" the experience.
